one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window: the FOMC on Oct 27-28 (Kalshi, Sep 30: 65% hold / 33% hike after the Fed hiked in September; a hold is mildly supportive for long-duration, high-multiple names) and Quanta's Q3 2026 report, expected Oct 29 (TIKR; the IR calendar does not show it yet, but Q3 2025 came on Oct 30). Earnings-day moves have been large in both directions: +17% after the Q2 2026 beat, which recovered a 22% slide, and down ~2.5% after a clean beat in Q3 2025. With consensus now reset higher after the Q2 raise and the key question being whether the 7.3% EBIT margin holds, I see no strong edge on direction. I used a near-symmetric lognormal centred on spot with a +0.4% drift, at 13% one-month vol: slightly above the 44%/3.5 = 12.6% baseline because earnings fall inside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of 30x P/E on Oct-2027 NTM adj. EPS of ~$22.3 (= $669) and 20x EV/EBITDA on NTM EBITDA of ~$5.14B less ~$5.0B net debt over 152.4M shares (= $642), weighted 60/40, which gives ~$658, roughly today's price. The multiples are set below today's ~35x and ~24x forward because multiples have historically mean-reverted and peers trade at 18-21x.

inputs_detail.derivation: Street 2028 estimate of ~$23.22 cited in search summary, consistent with 2027E $19.77 grown at management's ~18% adj. EPS CAGR target

Forward P/E history is 19x (2021), 21x (2022), 26x (2023), 31x (2024), 35x (2025), ~35x now, with a June 2026 peak of ~50x. Peers EME (~20x) and MTZ (~18x) trade much lower. Base rates say premium multiples compress as growth matures, so I used 30x: below today's 35x and above the 5-year average of ~28x, to credit the 18% EPS CAGR and $53B backlog.

PWR trades at ~24x forward EV/EBITDA today (TIKR, Aug 2026), and Wolfe used 27x on 2028 at a time of peak multiples. I assume some compression toward peers and history, in line with the 30x P/E choice
Starts from the reported Jun-30-2026 net debt of $5.6B and assumes part of the $2.0-2.5B FY26 FCF guidance goes to deleveraging after acquisitions and buybacks

bear.story: AI and hyperscaler capex gets cut or pushed out, or a 2027 recession hits (Polymarket puts a US recession by end-2027 at 35%; its 'AI downturn by Jun-2027' market is at ~18%). Multiples compress toward the EME/MTZ range of ~20-22x on ~$21 EPS. PWR's own history includes -23% to -29% down years (2008, 2015, 2018), a 22% one-month slide in Jul 2026, and -48%/-78% in the 2001-02 telecom bust, which is the closest analogue to an overbuild.

base.story: Backlog of $53B (+49% y/y) converts and EPS compounds ~17-18% toward ~$22-23 NTM by late 2027, while the forward P/E drifts from ~35x to ~30-31x. That leaves price roughly flat to up mid-single digits, as EPS growth is mostly absorbed by de-rating, which is the usual pattern for premium-multiple compounders after a 60% year.

bull.story: Large transmission and generation awards enter backlog in 2H26-2027, Q2's 7.3% EBIT margin proves structural, hyperscaler capex reaches ~$1.3T in 2027, and the multiple holds at ~38-40x NTM EPS of ~$23-24, near the Street-high targets (~$900-976).

thesis_break_reason: Around $450 the stock would trade near 20x NTM EPS, the peer and pre-2023 multiple. That would most likely mean the market sees earnings at risk (backlog cancellations or deferrals tied to cuts in data-center or utility capex, a margin reversal, or a 2027 recession), not just de-rating. It also sits well below the Jul-2026 panic low (~$560) and the 52-week low of $404.51 is close by.

reasoning: Anchor: PWR closed at $662.6, about 33.5x 2027 consensus EPS of $19.77 and ~35x forward, versus a forward P/E that rose from 19x in 2021 to 35x in 2025 and peaked near 50x in June 2026. Peers EME and MTZ trade at ~18-21x. EPS momentum is very strong: Q2 adj. EPS was $4.24 vs $3.31 expected, FY26 guidance was raised to $16.45-16.95, backlog is $53.4B, and management targets an ~18% EPS CAGR. My fundamental value (30x NTM EPS / 20x NTM EBITDA as of Oct-2027) is ~$658, roughly spot, because I assume EPS growth is largely offset by de-rating. That is the base rate for premium compounders after +60% years, and it matches the Jun-Sep 2026 pattern, when estimates rose ~27% while the forward P/E fell from ~50x to ~35x. Street targets average $769, about 16% above spot. History: PWR has risen every year from 2019 to 2026, but its down years were -23% to -29% and its last capex-overbuild bust (2001-02) cost -48% and then -78%. The macro event odds are fat-tailed: Polymarket gives 35% for a US recession by end-2027 (thin, ~$10k volume) and ~18% for an 'AI downturn by Jun-2027' ($3.0M volume), and Kalshi has the Fed on hold in October after a September hike. I built a three-scenario lognormal mixture: bear $440 (22%, 28% within-scenario vol), base $690 (55%, 20%) and bull $930 (23%, 20%). Its mean is ~$705 (+6%), its median is ~$680, and its spread is consistent with 44% realized vol plus a fat left tail.
